Read the guide
Getting started
Open the café, run time and find the tools for each decision.
Strategies to try
Test prices, stock and staffing, then see what changed.
Accounting and reports
Follow a purchase and a sale through the reports and journal.
Working capital and cash flow
Predict a shortfall and compare ways to cover it.

“Start café” creates the business. The game clock begins paused at 08:00. Tap ×1, ×5 or ×20 to start the clock. Customers arrive during trading hours (08:00–17:00). Pause stops the clock, and normal playback skips the closed hours. Use the café overview below the scene to check profit, groups served and why groups left.
Music and appearance
The Music menu on the café screen lets you choose a track or mute sound. Switch visual themes in Café → Settings during the same game.
Run a fair comparison

Let a few trading days finish. Change one thing and run a few more days. Use Price change results for the dish, the café overview for service losses, and Finance → P&L for gross profit and wages. Then check Forecast to see if the café can cover upcoming bills.
Test a price change

In Operations → Pricing, tap a price, adjust it and save. “Price change results” opens the changed dish at the top. It compares equal groups of completed days around the change. Try a small cut on a well-stocked dish or a price increase. Look at portions, sales and groups leaving without buying, then check gross profit in P&L.
Fix the bottleneck

Check the reasons for lost groups in the café overview. If products run out, check Inventory and buy what is missing. If goods repeatedly expire, order smaller batches. If the café repeatedly loses groups to service capacity, use Staff to compare the cost of the next shift with the gross profit on recoverable sales.
Management accounting

In Finance → P&L, compare Revenue, Groups served under Customer activity, and Sales per served group for the same periods. This helps you decide whether to focus on attracting more groups or improving what each group buys.
What the reports answer

In P&L, Month to date compares the current month so far with the same point of the previous month. Use it to see how this month is going. Closed months compares complete 30-day months when available. Use it to judge the final result once the full month’s costs are recorded.
Follow an invoice and a sale

Buy stock on credit in Operations → Purchasing. In Finance → Balance Sheet, tap Inventory or Supplier payables if marked ›. In Journal, select the day and open the invoice. Pay it in Bills and look for the supplier payment in Cash Flow. After a sale, tap Revenue or Cost of goods sold in P&L and open the related journal entries.
Spot the gap before payday

Working capital is current assets, such as cash and stock, minus short-term debts, such as supplier bills. In Finance → Forecast, compare bank and till and look for the first projected bank shortfall. Confirm the bill in Bills. To cover the gap with till money, use Deposit cash to bank in Forecast.
Compare ways to finance a gap

In Operations → Purchasing, check the payment term offered for each item. Deferral is 7 days for short-lived goods and 14 for others. Check Bills for the new date and Forecast for the expected bank balance. Keep enough stock for service and enough bank funds to pay on time.
Plan for the starter loan

The first instalment is due on day 31 and following instalments every 30 days. In Finance → Forecast, check upcoming cash needs. In Bills, review the last payment and open its journal entries. Use Balance Sheet for loan debt, P&L for interest expense, and Cash Flow for the payment.
Check the date and amount of the first projected bank shortfall. Compare bank and till funds, then open Bills to see what is due.
Save a change, then open Price change results at the top to compare completed days. Watch units, sales and customer losses.
Skip time

Open Skip at the top right of Café while time is paused. Use Next decision to advance to an event that needs attention, or Next day to review a shift. Skip processes sales, stock and payments along the way. With Next week, you cannot intervene in those days as they happen.

After changing a price or placing a large order, advance one day at a time. Check the café overview for stock shortages and groups leaving without buying. In Inventory, check Waste before ordering more perishables.
Move between screens

Use the bottom bar to switch between Café, Operations and Finance. Scene links can open a specific management tab. Operations has Pricing, Purchasing, Inventory and Staff. Finance has Forecast, Bills, P&L, Balance Sheet, Cash Flow and Journal.
Set prices and choose what to sell. Use Price change results at the top to see how sales and café traffic moved after a change. The strategy chapter shows how to test higher and lower prices.
Order products, check shelf life and choose immediate or deferred payment when offered. See Working capital for how payment dates change the bank forecast.
Compare usage, remaining stock and waste before placing another order. Open an ingredient to see its daily history. See Accounting for an example of adjusting the next order.
Use service capacity and staffing losses to decide whether another employee could help. Changes take effect the next day. In Strategies, see how to check if extra sales would cover the hire.
Check the first predicted bank shortfall, deposit till cash or review the credit line. Working capital walks through a cash shortage.
Find the due dates for supplier invoices, wages, rent, taxes and loan payments. Check which bills are due or overdue before spending the bank balance.

Compare profit, sales costs and expenses. Under Customer activity and Sales per served group, see why revenue changed. Open the margin breakdown to compare ingredients and dishes. See Accounting for how to read the period selector.
Check assets, debts and equity at each reporting date. Tap a row marked › to view its journal entries. See Accounting for a deferred purchase example.
See what brought cash in and what it paid for. Use this report for payments already made and Forecast for payments still ahead.
Find entries by date or account. Open a transaction to see its debits and credits. The accounting example follows a purchase, payment and sale.
At €4 per dish and €2 in ingredients, 30 sales leave €60 gross profit before other expenses.\nAt €3.50, you need 40 sales to match that €60. Prices in this example exclude VAT.
An extra employee costs €40 a day. At €2 gross profit per extra dish, the café needs 20 extra sales a day to cover that cost.
Revenue grows and sales per group stay around €10. If groups served rise from 100 to 120, the increase comes from serving more groups.

In Finance → P&L, open Margin breakdown. Compare portions by dish to see what changed in the sales mix, then compare the average cost of ingredients used in sales. Ingredient costs come from the stock actually consumed in each period. Use both tables to investigate a change in gross profit.
If ingredient costs are steady but more low-margin dishes sold, look at the menu mix. If the mix is similar and milk used in sales cost more per 100 ml, check milk purchases and pricing.

In Operations → Inventory, read Used, Waste and End together. An ingredient with high waste and stock left suggests smaller or less frequent orders. If stock hits zero and the overview shows lost sales, adjust what you buy. Open the ingredient to see which days it ran out or expired.
You bought 24 portions, used 12, discarded 8 and have 4 left. Try a smaller next order. If waste falls without more stock losses, the adjustment helped.
On day 38, Month to date compares day 31 through the current time on day 38 with the equivalent stretch of the first month. Use Closed months to see the full result for days 1–30.

Buy €120 on credit → debit Inventory €120, credit Supplier payables €120.\nPay €120 → debit Supplier payables, credit Bank. Cash falls by €120.\nSell a dish → sales and VAT appear in one entry. In the cost entry, the ingredients used move from Inventory to Cost of goods sold.
Bank €200 · Till €500 · Bill €600.\nMove €400 from the till to the bank before paying. The transfer changes where the money is held. Total cash drops only when the bill is paid.
A €300 order paid in seven days leaves €300 available today. In Forecast, check whether the €300 invoice and any wages or rent still fit on the due date.

Find Credit line under Finance → Forecast. If the forecast still shows a shortfall after reviewing stock purchases and till deposits, use the credit line for the amount needed and plan to repay it. Interest accrues daily on the outstanding draw. Check Forecast again after the draw.
If the gap is €250 and €1,000 is still available on the line, draw €250. When bank funds recover, consider repaying it after checking the next bills.
A €700 instalment has €600 of principal and €100 of interest.\nBank falls €700. Balance Sheet debt falls €600. The €100 interest is an expense in P&L in the period it accrues.
